findings.concern: The mandated "validate `body`, not just `tags` and `stem`" requirement has no mechanism available under the plan's own stated constraints, and no matching invariant or acceptance criterion.
findings.location: task/fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber § Work, item 1, bullet "Validate `body`, not just `tags` and `stem`" (vs. the closing "Invariants to hold" bullet and item 2's regression shapes)
findings.what_fails: Item 1's primary mechanism is a *pure, driver-side* validator ("a pure `validateFetchedRoadmap` (or a guard inside `buildReviewUnits`)"). The plan requires it to reject "a returned `body` that does not correspond to the real document", and explicitly forecloses the only two cheap escapes: it rules out an emptiness predicate ("Copy that guard's fail-closed *shape*, but not its predicate" — both recorded corruptions carried non-empty bodies) and it defers adding any further fetch agents. But the driver's ONLY source for the body is the payload being validated. The plan itself establishes there is no second source: "`args` is the ONLY deterministic input channel the Workflow runtime has ... a workflow script cannot run a command itself" — corroborated at `docs/workflow-schemas.md:64` (`process`/`fetch` are `undefined`) and `:1188` (no `child_process`, cannot shell out). For the roadmap payload there is at least a cross-field signal (the recorded corruption put the roadmap's real body into `phases[0].body` with `stem` = the roadmap slug, which the prescribed stem check already catches). For the single-unit task/phase branch — the round-2 corruption `{"body": "fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber task fetched successfully", "tags": ["plan-target"]}` — the payload has exactly two fields and no cross-field redundancy whatsoever, so body correspondence is not decidable by any pure function of it. The plan compounds this by never carrying the requirement forward: the closing "Invariants to hold, whatever the mechanism" list covers only tags and per-phase `ident`, and item 2's preferred regression enumerates only "garbage `tags`, a phase `stem` equal to the roadmap slug, a phase count that disagrees" — nothing asserts body validation. So the plan's most emphasized new requirement is the one thing it neither makes possible nor tests.
findings.why: This is not an implementer's decision to make — it is a requirement with an empty solution space, sitting next to invariants that silently omit it. The three available responses are all bad. (a) Skip the bullet: the plan's stated central claim ("a fabricated body is currently undetectable anywhere in the lane", "the validation must cover `body` as well as `tags`") goes unimplemented, and because no invariant or AC covers body, nothing in review or CI will notice — the task closes reporting success on a requirement it did not meet. (b) Invent a content heuristic (body length floor, "does it read like a sentence", slug-appears-in-body): a false positive fails closed and strands the item in `needs-plan-review` permanently, which is precisely the harm the plan argues against two bullets earlier for `phases`-emptiness ("no re-run could ever clear it, and ... it would accumulate undiagnosed") — the plan thus mandates a check whose only implementable forms reproduce a failure mode it elsewhere rules out. (c) Reach for a second agent to cross-check the body: directly contradicts the deferral in the same item. Independently verified as live scope, not already-fixed: `hoistedFetchedOk` (`.claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs:194`) guards only the caller-hoisted `parsed.fetched`; the agent-fetch fallback at `:789`/`:806` flows straight into `buildReviewUnits` (`:596`), whose only check is still the empty-body test at `:600`/`:628`. The gap is real — but the body half of the prescribed fix cannot be built as specified.
findings.recommendation: Split the body requirement from the tags/stem requirement and scope each to what is decidable. Keep item 1's tags/`stem`/phase-count checks as the fail-closed driver-side validation (these are decidable from cross-field disagreement within the roadmap payload, and are what the reported clobber actually needs). For `body`, either (i) drop it from item 1 and state explicitly that a fabricated body is out of scope for a pure driver-side guard, filing it as a follow-up against the fetch-prompt/hoist surface — noting the plan's own observation that finders re-read the real document themselves, so a fabricated body is decorative there and only the `tags` write is authoritative; or (ii) if it must be in scope, name the concrete source of truth it is checked against and how the driver obtains it without shelling out or adding an agent (e.g. require the caller-hoisted `args` path to supply body/tags and treat an agent-fetch fallback payload as unvalidatable-therefore-fail-closed-at-the-gate-only — clearing no tag while still reporting findings). Either way, add the corresponding entry to the "Invariants to hold" list and a matching assertion to item 2's regression, so the requirement is verifiable in whichever form survives.

findings.concern: coherence
findings.location: task/fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber § Work, item 1 — the "Validate `body`, not just `tags` and `stem`" bullet and the "applies to the PLAN_TARGET (task/phase) fetch" bullet
findings.what_fails: The plan makes driver-side validation the primary mechanism and then requires it to detect a fabricated `body` and a fabricated task-path `tags` list — neither of which any driver-side check can detect, because the driver has no independent access to the real document. The plan itself establishes this impossibility elsewhere in its own text: "`args` is the ONLY deterministic input channel the Workflow runtime has (`docs/workflow-schemas.md` § \"Import spike\": no `process`, no `fetch`, no `require`; a workflow script cannot run a command itself)". Every predicate the plan actually enumerates is structural and roadmap-only — "a phase `stem` equal to the roadmap slug, a missing/empty `stem`, a non-array `tags`, or a phase count that disagrees". Apply all four to the plan's own round-2 reproduction, `{"body": "fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber task fetched successfully", "tags": ["plan-target"]}`: there is no `phases` array, `tags` IS an array of strings, and there is no `stem`. Nothing fires. The plan's stated invariant — "after the gate runs, the item's tag list is exactly its pre-gate tags minus `needs-plan-review` — for every target type" — is therefore not reachable by the mechanism the plan prescribes, on the one target type the plan reproduced live.
findings.why: This is not a delegated implementation detail with equivalent branches; the branches produce different outcomes. An implementer following the enumerated predicates ships shape checks that catch the round-1 roadmap corruption and provably miss the round-2 task corruption, then marks the task done against an invariant the plan claims covers all target types. The plan's own analysis says a guard "must check values against something independently known rather than trusting a validated return" — and then supplies no independently-known source for `body` or for a task's `tags`. The one direction that could supply ground truth deterministically is mentioned only in passing, scoped to phases, and buried inside the deferred option: "tighten `buildRoadmapFetchPrompt` to return that `phases` summary array verbatim and validate against it — still one agent." Having the fetch agent echo `rdm ... show --format json` stdout verbatim and having the driver `JSON.parse` it is the generalization of that idea and would cover `body` and `tags` on every target type, but the plan never adopts it or names it as an option for the non-phase fields.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) name a mechanism that supplies ground truth to the driver — the natural one is to change the fetch prompts to return the raw `--format json` stdout verbatim as a single string and have the driver parse `body`/`tags`/`phases[].stem` out of it deterministically, so the agent transcribes nothing structured — or (b) scope the invariant honestly: state that driver-side shape/consistency validation covers the roadmap fan-out and stem corruption only, that a fabricated `body` or a fabricated task `tags` list remains undetectable in the fallback path, and record that residue as an explicit non-goal with a follow-up. Do not leave the invariant claiming all target types while the enumerated checks cover one.

findings.location: task/fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber § "Work" item 1, bullet "Validate `body`, not just `tags` and `stem`" vs. the closing "Invariants to hold, whatever the mechanism" bullet
findings.what_fails: The bullet requires detecting "a returned `body` that does not correspond to the real document", and the round-2 evidence section reinforces it ("any guard must check values against something independently known rather than trusting a validated return"). But on the agent-fetch fallback path — the only path this task is scoped to guard, per the plan's own "phase 3 hoists the path callers drive; this task guards the path they cannot" — the driver has no independently-known body. The plan itself establishes why: `args` is "the ONLY deterministic input channel the Workflow runtime has … a workflow script cannot run a command itself", and the plan separately forbids the `parallel()` fan-out that would add a second reader. That leaves only unstated options (a second cross-checking agent, or a shape heuristic such as rejecting a one-sentence body), which differ in cost and in what they catch. The plan then omits `body` entirely from its normative invariants, which cover only the post-gate tag list and per-phase `ident`s.
findings.why: This is not merely a delegated implementation decision: the plan asserts the requirement is mandatory ("nothing in the lane detects it today"), forecloses the obvious mechanism, supplies no alternative, and provides no criterion by which an implementer could demonstrate the requirement was met. An implementer will either add an arbitrary heuristic with no agreed bar, or quietly skip `body` — and because it is not an invariant, skipping it is invisible at review time. Both recorded incidents returned a fabricated non-empty `body`, so this is the one part of the observed failure that could silently ship unfixed.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) state a concrete, runtime-legal mechanism and make it testable — e.g. reject a `body` shorter than a stated floor, or one whose first line is a fetch-report sentence rather than a Markdown heading — and add a matching invariant ("a payload whose `body` fails the shape check is treated as a fetch failure, not gated"); or (b) explicitly downgrade `body` validation to out-of-scope for this task with a one-line rationale (the hoisted path carries a caller-read body; the agent path has no second source), and file the residual as a follow-up. Do not leave it as a mandatory requirement with no mechanism and no invariant.

findings.concern: coherence
findings.location: task/fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber § Work item 1, bullet "Validate `body`, not just `tags` and `stem`"
findings.what_fails: The plan mandates a fail-closed check on a `body` "that does not correspond to the real document", but specifies no predicate and the driver cannot obtain the real document to compare against. The plan itself establishes the impossibility three paragraphs later: `docs/workflow-schemas.md` § "Import spike" — no `process`, no `fetch`, no `require`; a workflow script cannot run a command itself. On the hoisted path the caller supplies the payload deterministically (so there is nothing to validate), and on the agent-fallback path the driver's only view of the document IS the payload under suspicion. Cross-checking a payload against itself detects nothing; the only mechanism that would work is a second independent fetch agent, which the plan's deferred-option bullet explicitly forbids ('must not reintroduce a `parallel()` fan-out', 'multiplies mechanical agents').
findings.why: This is not a cosmetic gap — it is the bullet that carries the round-2 incident. The recorded round-2 `fetch:task` payload is `{"body": "fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber task fetched successfully", "tags": ["plan-target"]}`. Trace it through every OTHER check the plan prescribes: `tags` is a valid non-empty string array (passes); there is no `stem` and no `phases` on the task path (both checks inapplicable); `body` is non-empty (passes). So the plan's implementable checks catch zero of the two incidents on the `--task` path, and the one bullet that would catch it is the unimplementable one. An implementer who follows the plan ships a guard, marks the task done, and the round-2 failure mode recurs unchanged — while the plan's own § Work invariant ("after the gate runs, the item's tag list is exactly its pre-gate tags minus `needs-plan-review` — for every target type") is asserted as met.
findings.recommendation: Decide the scope question the plan is currently straddling, because the two branches lead to different goals. Either (a) narrow item 1's stated goal to what a self-contained driver-side guard can actually achieve — structural disagreement on the roadmap path (`stem` equal to the roadmap slug, missing/empty `stem`, non-array `tags`) — and record explicitly that a fabricated-but-well-shaped task payload remains undetectable in-driver, closing that half by making the hoist mandatory for the `--task` path rather than optional; or (b) keep body/tags content validation as the goal and name the only mechanism that supports it (an independent second read), accepting the agent-count cost the deferred-option bullet currently rules out. Do not leave both in the plan — as written the two bullets contradict each other.

Step 2 is headed "Point the rewritten prose at the EXISTING `docs/principles.md`" — but its body only asks to verify coverage, and nothing in this repo currently names that path: `grep -rn 'principles\.md' CLAUDE.md .claude/workflows/ rdm-core/src/templates/ docs/workflow-schemas.md` returns zero, and the decision removes both the config key and the runtime argument that could have supplied it. So a `focus` string that hardcodes `docs/principles.md` ships an rdm path to every downstream consumer, while one that does not means the reviewer only ever reaches `docs/principles.md` if a repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md points there — which rdm's own CLAUDE.md does not. No acceptance criterion distinguishes the two: the zero-grep list is `rdm-core|anyhow|rustdoc|# Panics|# Safety`, which a literal `docs/principles.md` passes.
findings.why: The phase's whole channel for conventions is this one prose pointer. Which of the two forms ships decides whether the neutral reviewer reintroduces a repo-specific path, and whether rdm's own reviews consult `docs/principles.md` at all or silently keep relying on the CLAUDE.md fallback — different outcomes, not a free implementation choice.
findings.recommendation: State the choice explicitly in step 1. Recommended: keep the prose path-free (copy `architectural-fit` verbatim in shape) and, in step 2, add the pointer to rdm's own `CLAUDE.md` instead — a one-line "the project's principles live in `docs/principles.md`" — so the generic prose resolves to the right file here without shipping an rdm path downstream. Then rewrite step 2's heading to match what it actually asks for (verify coverage; add only the same-commit clause to §13), and add an AC asserting the fallback chain appears in the shipped prose.

Reading A (literal step 2) writes the operator-supplied path `docs/principles.md` into `lib/review.mjs` prose, which is stamped into three workflow consumers and rendered into `skill-review-{cli,mcp}.md` — files that SHIP. A downstream repo has no `docs/principles.md`, and if the operator ran `rdm agent-config --principles-file CONVENTIONS.md`, the emitted skill would carry BOTH the substituted `## Principles / Read CONVENTIONS.md` note (agent_config.rs:368) and dimension prose saying to read `docs/principles.md` — contradictory instructions in one file. Reading B (generic step 1) is portable but leaves step 2's premise unimplementable: nothing points at `docs/principles.md`, and because `WorkflowFile` is emitted verbatim with NO substitution pass (agent_config.rs:231-238), a workflow-lane reviewer has no configured principles note at all and falls back to CLAUDE.md — which nowhere references `docs/principles.md` (grep over CLAUDE.md returns zero). Under reading B the §13 same-commit edit in step 2 is inert. No acceptance criterion discriminates: AC1 bans only 'crate name, language name, or language-specific doc-section name', and the AC2 grep is `rdm-core|anyhow|rustdoc|# Panics|# Safety` — `docs/principles.md` trips neither.

findings.recommendation: State explicitly in step 1 that the rewritten prose names NO path and copies architectural-fit's wording verbatim ('the project's principles (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md if no principles note is configured)'). Retitle step 2 to what its body actually does — verify coverage in docs/principles.md, no second document, add only the §13 same-commit clause — and drop the 'point the prose at' imperative. Add a negative AC: `grep -n 'docs/principles' .claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs` returns zero. If rdm's own workflow-lane reviewer is meant to read docs/principles.md, the correct channel is a pointer FROM CLAUDE.md (which the prose does name), not a path baked into shipped prose.

findings.concern: The "Read-but-no-match is a confident false" acceptance criterion asserts a dimension set the plan's own untouched-invariants make unreachable
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — "Read-but-no-match is a confident false"
findings.what_fails: An implementer writes the AC's test verbatim: `selectDimensions('code', deriveSignals({ changedFiles: ['src/util/helper.js'], diffText: '+  const x = 1;\n' }))` and asserts it equals `['ac','correctness']`. The two available exits are both bad: ship a red gate, or satisfy it by weakening `changesLogic`/`missingTests` derivation — which contradicts the phase's own invariants and silently removes the `tests` dimension from every code review. This AC is also the one the phase designates as the guard that keeps fail-open from widening, so it is load-bearing rather than incidental.
findings.recommendation: Restate the criterion in terms of the three conditional signals only, and pin the dimension set to what the untouched signals actually produce. E.g.: `deriveSignals({ changedFiles: ['src/util/helper.js'], diffText: '+  const x = 1;\n' })` leaves `publicApiChanged`, `userFacing`, and `securitySurface` all `false`, and `selectDimensions('code', …)` returns exactly `['ac','correctness','tests']` — containing none of `api-docs`, `changelog`, `security`. If an exact-equality-on-`['ac','correctness']` assertion is wanted, seed the fixture with a changed test file alongside the code file (clearing `missingTests`) — but note `changesLogic` alone still fires `tests`, so no code-file fixture can ever reach `['ac','correctness']`.

findings.concern: Acceptance criterion 1 forbids a `\bpub\b` content clause that step 2 requires in the export vocabulary

findings.concern: architectural-fit
findings.location: Steps §3 ("Make it genuinely absent so the `signals == null` fail-open path engages"), Operator decision bullet 2, and the AC "With content that decides nothing, an undeterminable signal does not resolve to a confident false"
findings.what_fails: The prescribed mechanism — omitting a per-signal key so `selectDimensions`' fail-open engages — cannot produce fail-open, and violates two stated architectural invariants the same plan requires to be preserved. `selectDimensions` fails open on the WHOLE object only (`.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs:1053` — `if (signals == null) return dims.slice();`); a returned object with a missing key is an explicit signals object, so each conditional predicate evaluates `!!s.publicApiChanged` / `!!s.userFacing` / `!!(s.securitySurface || s.hasUnsafe)` (review.mjs:227, 240, 254) against `undefined` → falsy → the dimension is DROPPED. That is fail-CLOSED — bit-for-bit the silent-skip defect the phase exists to remove. It also contradicts the explicitly documented `deriveSignals` invariant (review.mjs:1100-1107 and docs/workflow-schemas.md's `deriveSignals(input)` section, currently :1099-1108: "every boolean key in SIGNAL_KEYS is set explicitly. A partially-populated object would make a conditional dimension drop out on a *missing* key rather than a real negative") — which is the exact failure mode being reintroduced. It is additionally pinned by a harness assertion the plan does not list for rewrite: `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh:1385-1387` loops `for (const key of SIGNAL_KEYS) assert.equal(typeof d1[key], 'boolean', …)`, so absence turns that gate red for every signal, not just the no-input `deepEqual` at :1400-1410 the plan does schedule for rewrite. Meanwhile the plan forbids the only edits that could make absence fail open: "`selectDimensions`' three-way fail-open contract is unchanged" (AC), and the `when` predicates are never mentioned as in scope.
findings.why: The plan treats per-key absence and whole-object absence as the same thing. They are different branches of a contract that review.mjs and docs/workflow-schemas.md both call out as load-bearing and deliberately distinct ("Omitted signals and an empty signals object are deliberately different paths"). Under the current `!!s.x` predicates, tri-state values are unrepresentable — `undefined` and `false` are indistinguishable to a selector, so absence cannot carry "unknown, run it anyway" without changing the selector.
findings.recommendation: Pick one mechanism explicitly in the plan rather than leaving it to implementation. (a) Fail-open BY VALUE, no shape change: an undeterminable signal resolves to `true`, keeping `deriveSignals` fully-populated-boolean, `selectDimensions` untouched, and :1385-1387 green — this satisfies the AC's actual requirement ("proven by a test asserting the dimension is still selected") with the smallest blast radius. Or (b) genuine tri-state: change each conditional `when` from `!!s.x` to `s.x !== false`, and state as in-scope that SIGNAL_KEYS' explicit-boolean invariant, `verify-workflow-review.sh:1385-1387`, and the docs/workflow-schemas.md fully-populated paragraph are all being amended — that is a change to the dimension-selection contract, which the current AC set forbids, so the AC must be reworded too. Either way, add `verify-workflow-review.sh`'s SIGNAL_KEYS boolean-typing loop to step 5's re-fixture list; the plan currently names only the no-input `deepEqual`.

findings.concern: architectural-fit
findings.location: Steps §3 ("Scope the policy: 'undeterminable' applies only when the diff actually touches code files (`codeFiles.length > 0`)"), §4's "The undeterminable/fail-open rule from step 3 applies to `securitySurface` too", and the security / `webpack.config.js` acceptance criteria
findings.what_fails: The undeterminable set is scoped by CODE-FILE PRESENCE, not by content-decidability, so for any diff containing a code file every content-derived signal that did not positively match is undeterminable. Combined with the fail-open intent, that selects `api-docs`, `changelog`, and `security` on EVERY code diff — the conditional dimensions stop being conditional. Two of the plan's own acceptance criteria then become unsatisfiable simultaneously: the security AC requires that "a diff touching `src/auth/session.js` with no sink-shaped content does NOT trigger" (a code file, no matching content → undeterminable → security selected → AC fails), and the `webpack.config.js` AC pins that file to the same `userFacing` value as `src/util/helper.js` — both code files with no user-facing content, so both undeterminable, so `changelog` fires on both. The plan states the policy "cannot widen into 'run every dimension on every diff'" and offers the docs-only carve-out as the guard, but a docs-only diff is the only case the carve-out excludes; every real code review lands in the widened set. This contradicts the stated architecture of the fleet in the canonical source itself (review.mjs:91-94: "Scale the fleet to what the change actually touches… This keeps a 10-line change cheap while a cross-cutting change still gets full coverage"), and pulls against the per-unit refutation budget CLAUDE.md describes as the cost bound on this same pipeline.
findings.why: "Content decided nothing" is conflated with "content could not be read." A populated `diffText` with no exported-symbol/sink/user-facing token is evidence of a genuine negative — the same class of evidence as a docs-only diff — not an absence of evidence. Scoping on `codeFiles.length > 0` cannot tell those apart, so it classifies every non-matching code diff as unknown.
findings.recommendation: Redefine "undeterminable" by decidability of the INPUT, not by file kind: a signal is undeterminable when `diffText === null` (or the diff was truncated/unavailable) while code files changed; when a non-null `diffText` is present and no content pattern matches, that is a legitimate `false`. That keeps the docs-only carve-out, makes both callers' populated-`diffText` path yield real negatives, preserves the triggered/always-on split, and makes the security and `webpack.config.js` ACs satisfiable as written. State that reading in step 3 and in the operator decision, and re-word the AC "With content that decides nothing…" so its scenario is a code diff with an unavailable/truncated `diffText`, not merely a non-matching one.

findings.concern: Steps 2 and 3 freeze a literal token-level pattern vocabulary for `publicApiChanged` and `userFacing`, which is an implementation decision the acceptance criteria already pin behaviorally — and two of the frozen tokens contradict the plan's own requirements.
findings.location: phase-3-generic-diff-signals, Steps 2 and 3 (the `export` / `module.exports` / `pub(crate)` / `public` / Go-capitalized-func / `__all__` list, and the `add_argument` / `addOption` / `.arg(` / `.command(` / `.flag(` / `app.get(` / `router.post(` / `@app.route` / `.route(` / `addTool(` / `console.log` / `console.error` / `print(` / `println!` / `eprintln!` list)
findings.what_fails: The plan dictates the exact regex vocabulary rather than the signal's contract. The acceptance criteria already constrain the behavior with executable fixtures — `+export function foo()` on `src/api/index.ts` must yield `publicApiChanged: true`; `+  program.option("--verbose", "print more output");` must yield `userFacing: true`; `+  const x = a + b;` must yield `false` — so the token list adds no risk reduction, only frozen surface. Two of the frozen tokens are actively wrong against the plan's own text: (a) step 3 requires `userFacing` be "a real discriminator, not a blanket true", but `console.log` / `console.error` / `print(` / `println!` appear in internal debug logging in a large fraction of ordinary code diffs, so implementing the list as written pushes `userFacing` toward the blanket-true the same step forbids; (b) `.arg(` is the same token in clap's CLI builder (`Command::new("x").arg(Arg::new("v"))`) and in `std::process::Command` (`Command::new("git").arg("status")`), so it collides head-on with step 5's process/command-execution security vocabulary — a diff adding `+  cmd.arg("--force");` would register as a user-facing CLI surface change.
findings.why: Step 5 — the harder of the three signals — deliberately stays at category altitude ("process/command execution, filesystem access, environment and secret reads, deserialization, raw memory access") and names no tokens, and is not weaker for it. The plan therefore demonstrates the correct altitude and then abandons it for the two easier signals. Whoever implements this will be tuning patterns against the harness fixtures anyway; a token list embedded in the plan cannot be tuned without the plan reading as violated, and the two defective tokens above show why that matters: the enumeration is now itself a thing needing review, which is exactly the surface-for-its-own-sake failure.
findings.recommendation: Cut steps 2 and 3 back to the altitude step 5 already uses: name the CATEGORIES (`publicApiChanged` — added lines introducing an exported/public symbol in the languages `CODE_EXTENSIONS` covers; `userFacing` — added lines registering a CLI flag/subcommand, an HTTP/RPC route, or emitting a user-visible message) and keep step 3's "must be a real discriminator, not a blanket true" requirement plus the existing positive/negative acceptance fixtures. If any examples are kept, mark them explicitly as illustrative rather than as the specification, and drop `console.log`/`print(`/`println!` and the bare `.arg(` from them so the plan does not hand the implementer a vocabulary that conflicts with its own discriminator requirement and with step 5.

findings.concern: Two rationales are each restated five times across Context, Operator decision, Steps, and Acceptance Criteria, and Step 1 asks for an audit whose conclusions the Context section has already fixed.
findings.location: phase-3-generic-diff-signals, Step 1; and the `mcp`/`config` and `\bpub\b` rationales repeated throughout Context / Operator decision / Steps 3-5 / Acceptance Criteria
findings.what_fails: The `mcp`/`config` spelling-coincidence rationale appears at Context bullet 3, Operator decision bullet 1, step 3, step 4's symmetric paragraph, step 5 ("for the same reason the `mcp`/`config` patterns go"), and the no-confident-TRUE acceptance criterion — six statements of one fact, plus a seventh in the roadmap's own Problem §4. findings.concern: coherence
findings.location: phase-3-generic-diff-signals — step 4, bullet 2 ("Content was actually READ (`diffText` non-null) and no pattern matched → a legitimate, confident `false`") and the AC "Read-but-no-match is a confident false"; the fail-open branch in step 4 bullet 4 and its AC "Undeterminable fails open by value"
findings.what_fails: Step 4 equates `diffText !== null` with "the content was read", but the diff both drivers feed in is TRUNCATED to the first 40000 characters (`dispatch-phase.js:2396-2397`, `review-refute-fix.js:1616-1617`, and the same truncation on the ABSORBED `IMPLEMENT_RESULT` path). Once path derivation is deleted, any change whose exported symbol or sink lands past that bound yields "read, no match" → a confident `false`, and `api-docs` / `security` / `changelog` silently never fire — in rdm's own repo as much as elsewhere. Meanwhile the compensating fail-open branch this phase invents (`diffText === null` with code files present) is effectively UNREACHABLE from either driver: `DIFF_SIGNALS_SCHEMA` and `IMPLEMENT_RESULT_SCHEMA` both list `diffText` as `required: [...]` of `type: 'string'` (dispatch-phase.js:2115-2120, :2136-2141), and when the diff agent fails or returns no files, both drivers omit the `signals` key wholesale before `deriveSignals` is ever called (`review-refute-fix.js`'s `if (changedFiles.length === 0)` branch, and dispatch-phase's identical one). So the plan spends its whole new safety mechanism, plus a dedicated AC, on a dead branch while the reachable degradation is classified as a genuine negative.
findings.why: This reintroduces the exact defect the phase exists to remove — a review that completes, reports clean, and has silently skipped a dimension — by a different route, and it is a REGRESSION relative to today for `userFacing`/`securitySurface`, which currently derive from `changedFiles` (never truncated) and are therefore truncation-immune. The existing code comment at `dispatch-phase.js:2109-2112` states the invalidated premise outright — "truncation only weakens trigger detection toward FAIL-OPEN (a missed trigger costs a dimension that would have run anyway when the file paths already imply it)" — and `docs/workflow-schemas.md:1117-1118` repeats it. That justification is exactly the path fallback this phase deletes, and no plan step retires either claim. Step 8 compounds it: it forbids editing the two call sites and freezes the input shape, and instructs the implementer to "stop and escalate" if a new input is needed — so an implementer following the plan as written has no sanctioned route to the fix.
findings.recommendation: Decide the truncation policy IN this plan, and name which surface owns it. Cheapest option inside the frozen input shape: have `deriveSignals` treat a `diffText` at or above the prompt's truncation bound as undeterminable (fail open by value), with the bound single-sourced as a named const in `lib/review.mjs` that the two prompt builders quote — this keeps step 8's no-call-site-edit rule intact. Alternative: let the drivers pass `diffText: null` when their output hit the bound, and lift step 8's call-site freeze explicitly for that one line. Either way add an AC pinning a >bound diff whose only trigger sits in the truncated tail, and add `dispatch-phase.js:2109-2112` plus `docs/workflow-schemas.md:1117-1118` to step 9's update list — both now assert the opposite of the new behavior and no gate greps them.

findings.concern: coherence
findings.location: phase-3-generic-diff-signals — step 4, bullet 3 ("**No code files** (`codeFiles.length === 0`) → confident `false`, regardless of `diffText`"), the Context line "`CODE_EXTENSIONS` is already multi-language and correct — leave it", and the AC "`CODE_EXTENSIONS` is untouched"
findings.what_fails: `CODE_EXTENSIONS` (`lib/review.mjs:1064`) is `['.rs','.js','.mjs','.cjs','.ts','.tsx','.py','.go','.sh','.pkl']` — it has no `.java`, `.rb`, `.c`, `.cpp`, `.cs`, `.php`, `.kt`, `.swift`, `.jsx`, `.vue`, `.tf`, `.sql`. Step 4 newly routes `publicApiChanged`, `userFacing`, and `securitySurface` through `codeFiles.length === 0`, a gate they do not consult today (`lib/review.mjs:1135-1138` are path-pattern reads with no code-file precondition). In a Ruby, Java, C#, or C++ repo every diff has `codeFiles.length === 0`, so all three signals resolve to a confident `false` on EVERY change and only `ac` + `correctness` ever run — permanently, silently. That is strictly worse than today, where such a repo touching `app/auth/session.rb` at least trips `securitySurface` via the path list.
findings.why: The roadmap's stated purpose is a lane that works outside rdm's repo, and this phase is named the most dangerous category because it degrades rather than fails. Declaring `CODE_EXTENSIONS` correct-and-untouched by AC while simultaneously making it authoritative for three more signals hard-codes a new language allowlist in place of the removed path allowlist — the same defect shape, one layer down. No acceptance criterion exercises a language outside the list, so every gate stays green while the lane is silently inert for a large class of repos.
findings.recommendation: Invert the docs-only test rather than widening the allowlist: define the genuine-negative carve-out as "every changed file matches a known NON-code extension (`.md`, `.txt`, `.rst`, images, …)" instead of "no file matches `CODE_EXTENSIONS`", and treat an unrecognized extension as undeterminable (fail open by value, per step 4 bullet 4). That keeps the three docs-only assertions the plan protects (`verify-workflow-review.sh` (c), `verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh`, `verify-workflow-dispatch.sh` round 1) green as written, since they all use `docs/*.md`. Add an AC pinning a `.rb`- or `.java`-only diff with sink-shaped content to `securitySurface: true`. If instead you keep the current gate, drop the "already multi-language and correct" claim and say plainly that the lane is scoped to those ten extensions.

findings.concern: restraint
findings.location: phase-3-generic-diff-signals — step 3's enumerated `userFacing` vocabulary (in particular the "user-visible output: printed or logged messages … `console.log`/`console.error`, `print(`, `println!`, `eprintln!`" bullet), and step 5's parallel token taxonomy
findings.what_fails: The plan hands the implementer a concrete API-token list per signal (`add_argument`, `addOption`, `.arg(`, `.command(`, `.flag(`, `app.get(`, `router.post(`, `@app.route`, `addTool(`, `console.log`, `print(`, `println!`, `eprintln!`, plus the export forms in step 2), and then, one paragraph later, imposes the real requirement: "This must be a real discriminator, not a blanket true." The prescribed list defeats that requirement — an added `console.log`/`println!` debug line is one of the most common lines in any diff, internal refactors included, so `userFacing` would read `true` on most code diffs and `changelog` would run almost unconditionally, demanding a CHANGELOG entry for internal-only work. The plan's only negative fixture (`+  const x = a + b;`) cannot catch this.
findings.why: This is the over-specified shape: the acceptance criteria already pin the observable contract (positive CLI-registration case true, internal-arithmetic case false, `webpack.config.js` identical to `src/util/helper.js`), which is the right level for a plan. Spelling out the token list adds no risk reduction — it adds a decision the implementer must now either follow into a known-bad trigger or silently override, plus more surface for the next reviewer to re-litigate.
findings.recommendation: Keep the requirement and the ACs; demote the token lists to "illustrative, not exhaustive — tune against the ACs". Separately, either drop generic logging calls from the `userFacing` vocabulary (a printed string is user-visible output only when it is part of the program's declared interface, which a grep cannot tell), or add a negative AC pinning `deriveSignals({ changedFiles: ['src/util/helper.js'], diffText: '+  console.log("cache miss", key);\n' })` to `userFacing: false`, so the discriminator claim is actually gated.

findings.concern: Step 3's 'genuinely absent signal engages the `signals == null` fail-open path' is mechanically impossible against the `selectDimensions` the plan simultaneously requires to stay unchanged; the two acceptance criteria are mutually unsatisfiable.
findings.location: Step 3 / Operator decision bullet 2 / AC 'With content that decides nothing, an undeterminable signal does not resolve to a confident false — proven by a test asserting the dimension is still selected' vs AC "`selectDimensions`' three-way fail-open contract is unchanged, with its existing tests still passing"
findings.what_fails: `selectDimensions` fail-opens only on the WHOLE signals object being null (`.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs:1053`), while each conditional dimension tests one key by truthiness (`when: (s) => !!s.publicApiChanged`, :227; `!!s.userFacing`, :240; `!!(s.securitySurface || s.hasUnsafe)`, :254). Omitting a key from a non-null object therefore yields `!!undefined` === false and the dimension is skipped — bit-for-bit the same silent skip this phase exists to eliminate, only spelled `undefined` instead of `false`. Making an absent key select the dimension instead requires changing those predicates (or `selectDimensions`), and since `{}` IS the all-keys-absent object, that promotes `{}` from 'computed, nothing triggered' to 'run every dimension' — which breaks the second leg of the three-way contract and turns `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh:1330-1334` (`assert.deepEqual(selectDimensions('code', {}).map(d => d.key), ['ac','correctness'])`) red, an existing test the plan's own AC requires to keep passing. The remaining escape — having `deriveSignals` return `null` wholesale whenever any conditional signal is undeterminable — contradicts the `webpack.config.js` AC, which asserts `userFacing` 'takes whatever value step 3's policy dictates, identically to a diff touching only `src/util/helper.js`' (a per-key value inside an object, not a null return), and would run all seven dimensions on essentially every code-touching diff, which is exactly the widening step 3 forbids.
findings.why: This is the phase's central mechanism, not a detail: 'undeterminable is not false' is what replaces the deleted `rdm-core/src/` gate for `publicApiChanged`, and it is also the fallback step 3 assigns to `userFacing` and step 4 to `securitySurface`. An implementer following the plan as written picks one of three branches with materially different outcomes — a silently-skipped `api-docs` dimension (the original defect, preserved), a rewritten `selectDimensions` contract the plan declares load-bearing and off-limits, or an always-fail-open pipeline. Step 8 shows the plan is aware of the tension (it asks the implementer to document 'the revised relationship' to the fully-populated invariant at `docs/workflow-schemas.md:1099-1107`) but never decides it, leaving the deciding question to be answered downstream of the code being written.
findings.recommendation: Name the mechanism in the plan and re-scope the conflicting AC. Concretely, pick one: (a) tri-state per key — conditional `when` predicates become `(s) => s.publicApiChanged !== false`, and the plan explicitly states the new meaning of `{}` and rewrites `verify-workflow-review.sh:1330-1334` rather than asserting it passes unmodified; (b) a dedicated sentinel (e.g. `publicApiChanged: 'unknown'`) that the predicates treat as triggering, leaving `{}` semantics and the existing test untouched — this appears to satisfy every other AC in the phase, including the `webpack.config.js` per-key comparison and the docs-only negative; or (c) keep booleans and drop the absence requirement. Then update the `selectDimensions`-unchanged AC to say precisely which leg is preserved (the `signals == null` → ALL leg) and which, if any, is being redefined, and extend step 8's doc update to the same decision.

findings.concern: `userFacing` is stripped of every input it has but never given a replacement definition, and its acceptance criterion is circular, so no implementation can fail it.
findings.location: Step 2 final sentence ('The same rule applies to `userFacing`: derive it from content, not from path spelling') + Step 3 + AC 'Given a synthetic non-rdm diff whose content is user-facing, `userFacing` is true and the `changelog` dimension is selected'
findings.what_fails: `USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS` (`review.mjs:1093-1098`) has exactly four members and the plan removes all four — `^rdm-cli\//` and `^rdm-server\//` by AC1's no-rdm-literal rule, `mcp` and `config` by step 3 — leaving `userFacing: lower.some(...)` with an empty list, i.e. permanently false. The plan specifies the replacement content shape for the other two rebuilt signals (`publicApiChanged`: 'added lines introducing an exported/public symbol'; `securitySurface`: 'process/command execution, filesystem access, environment and secret reads, deserialization, raw memory access') but gives `userFacing` none. Its AC is then self-referential — 'a diff whose content is user-facing ⇒ `userFacing` is true' — so whatever heuristic the implementer invents, they also author the fixture that satisfies it; the criterion cannot discriminate a good implementation from a stub that returns the sentinel unconditionally. Step 3's wording ('drop the generic `mcp`/`config` patterns FROM `USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS`') also reads as though the list survives with its two rdm members, which AC1 forbids; that is resolvable by deleting the list, but the plan never says so.
findings.why: `userFacing` is the sole trigger for the `changelog` dimension (`when: (s) => !!s.userFacing`, `review.mjs:240`), and the plan's own final AC notes that dimension treats a missing changelog entry as `blocking`. 'User-facing' is also the least content-derivable of the three signals — there is no language-neutral token shape for it comparable to `export`/`pub` or `exec`/`spawn` — so the gap is where the phase's method is weakest, not merely where its prose is thinnest. Two implementers will ship different downstream gate behavior and both will pass this AC.
findings.recommendation: Either (i) state the content shape for `userFacing` at the same specificity as the other two — e.g. added lines touching CLI argument/flag declarations, printed or logged output strings, HTTP route or handler registrations, exported config schema keys — and rewrite the AC to pin a concrete fixture and path the way the security AC does (`src/lib/runner.js` + `+const { exec } = require('child_process')`); or (ii) decide that user-facing-ness is not content-derivable, route `userFacing` to the undeterminable branch whenever `codeFiles.length > 0`, and say so explicitly. Either way, state that `USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS` is deleted outright rather than pruned.

findings.concern: The closing 'Open structural questions' section contradicts the Operator decision that supersedes it, and points the implementer at a still-open task whose sanctioned resolutions include the opposite of step 4 and its acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Trailing section 'Open structural questions (filed as tasks, not resolved here)' vs 'Operator decision (2026-07-25) — content, not declared paths'

Pinning `securitySurface` to path-only directly violates step 4 and the AC requiring that `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` no longer exist and that a repo-wide grep return no hits. findings.concern: The `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` acceptance criterion ('a repo-wide grep for it returns no hits') collides with step 8's instruction to document that symbol's removal by name.
findings.location: AC 'Conversely `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` no longer exists: a repo-wide grep for it returns no hits' vs Step 8 ('Update the `deriveSignals(input)` section … that `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` is gone')
findings.what_fails: Step 8 requires `docs/workflow-schemas.md` to record that `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` is gone, and step 5 requires re-fixturing the harness assertions that currently reference it; a changelog entry describing the behavior change is likely to name it too. The same wording also catches `review.mjs:1061-1062`'s surviving comment block if it still mentions the list.

findings.concern: Step 3's 'genuinely absent signal engages selectDimensions' fail-open' mechanism does not exist at key granularity, and every route to it collides with an acceptance criterion this same phase freezes
findings.location: Steps 3 and 4; ACs "an undeterminable signal does not resolve to a confident false" and "selectDimensions' three-way fail-open contract is unchanged" — vs. .claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs:227,240,254,1050-1059
findings.what_fails: `selectDimensions` fails open only on the WHOLE object (review.mjs:1053 — `if (signals == null) return dims.slice()`). Per-key absence engages nothing: the conditional predicates are `!!s.publicApiChanged` (:227), `!!s.userFacing` (:240), `!!(s.securitySurface || s.hasUnsafe)` (:254), so an absent key coerces to false and the dimension is filtered out at :1054 — exactly the confident-false this phase exists to remove, respelled. All three escapes are closed by the phase's own ACs: (a) relaxing a `when` to `s.x !== false` breaks scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh:1329-1334 (`selectDimensions('code', {})` deepEqual `['ac','correctness']`), which the AC "selectDimensions' three-way fail-open contract is unchanged, with its existing tests still passing" forbids; (b) returning `null` for the whole object discards the determinable negatives on any code diff and runs every dimension, which the AC "the fail-open policy cannot widen into always running every dimension" forbids; (c) leaving the key `undefined` inside a still-returned object breaks verify-workflow-review.sh:1385-1387 (`typeof d1[key] === 'boolean'` for every SIGNAL_KEYS entry), an assertion step 5 never lists for rewrite. The AC "proven by a test asserting the dimension is still selected" is therefore unsatisfiable as specified.
findings.why: The three-way contract at review.mjs:1034-1059 is declared load-bearing by CLAUDE.md and by this phase itself ("Do not weaken it"). The plan asserts an interaction with that contract that the code does not provide, so the implementer must either weaken the contract (violating a stated architectural constraint) or fail an AC. The most likely silent outcome is shipping `undefined` where `false` was — no observable change, but it reads as a fix.
findings.recommendation: Settle the mechanism in the plan before implementation: either (i) introduce an explicit third value (e.g. a `null`/`'unknown'` marker) plus a documented four-way evaluation rule so an explicit unknown selects the dimension while a missing key still reads false — which keeps `{}` meaning "computed, nothing triggered" and leaves :1329-1334 green; or (ii) drop the absence notion and pin each signal to a defensible content-derived boolean. Either way add ACs covering SIGNAL_KEYS population (verify-workflow-review.sh:1385-1387) and docs/workflow-schemas.md's "every boolean key is set explicitly" invariant, which step 8 only gestures at.

findings.concern: The blast-radius analysis omits the skill-prose projection CLAUDE.md names as review.mjs's co-equal second `--check`-gated output, whose trigger prose describes exactly the triggers this phase replaces
findings.location: Steps 6 and 8, and the "Blast radius" section — vs. CLAUDE.md's two-projection statement and review.mjs:218,242 → rdm-core/src/templates/skill-review-cli.md:143,153
findings.what_fails: CLAUDE.md states lib/review.mjs "has TWO `--check`-gated projections": gen-workflow-review.sh stamps the JS block, and gen-skill-review.sh renders the `//|` spec prose into four shipped skill templates. That prose carries the trigger descriptions this phase invalidates — review.mjs:218 `//|code| - **api-docs** — *trigger: the diff changes a public \`rdm-core\` item.*` and :242 `//|code| - **security** — *trigger: the diff touches auth, input parsing or validation, path/file handling, subprocess or shell invocation…*` — rendered verbatim into skill-review-cli.md:143 and :153 (plus the -mcp and .claude/skills/rdm-review/SKILL.md copies). Phase 1 owns dimension prose generally, but it runs first and cannot describe content triggers phase 3 has not yet introduced.

Separately, disambiguate the first AC's "or any stamped consumer": the api-docs `focus` string (review.mjs:224) contains a literal `rdm-core` inside the stamped block, so a literal grep over stamped consumers cannot pass in this phase — scope that AC to `deriveSignals` and its pattern lists and leave the focus prose to phase 1.

findings.concern: Every harness line number cited is stale by roughly 500-550 lines, including the one line range step 5 issues a direct edit instruction against and the three ranges marked MUST-NOT-TOUCH
